newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No need to brake Brazil economy now - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: No need to brake Brazil economy now - cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank sees no current need to slam the brakes on credit but is committed to economic stability and will take whatever measures necessary to safeguard that stability, a Central Bank director said.
Francisco Lopes, Director of Monetary Policy, said Thursday's meeting of the National Monetary Council (CMN) did not discuss possible credit curbs and he did not think them necessary "for now."
"We are always monitoring the economy. We have a commitment to austerity which is necessary to guarantee economic stability," Lopes told reporters after the CMN meeting.
"When we consider it opportune, we will make decisions, even if they are unpopular, if we think them necessary to maintain stability," he added.
Economists are predicting that new restrictions on credit could be introduced in about three weeks time to curb import growth and plug a widening trade gap.
